idea: Week three, from the story bank: written from the source, then corrected by two independent editors before voicing.
description: Rajasthan generated 59,921 of India's 1,74,757 million units of solar electricity in FY 2025-26: 34%, or one unit in three, and 2.2 times Gujarat's 27,380. It was over twice the next state in each financial year from 2022-23 to 2025-26.

In FY 2021-22 its share was 23.4%. Generation as reported by the Central Electricity Authority; state totals, not per person. Given by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy in a Lok Sabha answer of 29 July 2026.
source: Central Electricity Authority (CEA), as given by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Government of India, in its reply to Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 1668 of 29 July 2026 (Renewable Energy Capacity), Annexure-II: State/UT-wise electricity generation from renewable sources by financial year, in million units (the answer: 'as per the information received from Central Electricity Authority'; source line under the table: Central Electricity Authority). The Solar column is used, for FY 2022-23 to FY 2025-26 (and FY 2021-22 for one earlier figure). The answer also prints FY 2026-27 up to May 2026, a part-year that is not used. The cards read 35 rows a year and the map all 36; the Total row printed in each table is the total used for the shares, and the rows add up to 99.99% of it or better. Cross-check: the answer of 18 March 2026 (Unstarred Question No. 4279, Solar Energy Generation in Andhra Pradesh) prints Rajasthan 198,370.95 of 634,412.72 million units over the last five financial years and the current year to January 2026. State totals, not per-person figures.
